findings.title: totalPages off by one when user_count is a multiple of limit
findings.body:
`totalPages` is computed as `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`. When the member count divides evenly by the limit (e.g. 50 members with limit 50), this reports 2 pages instead of 1.

Consequences:
- The UI shows `1/2`.
- `showingLast` is false on the real last page, so the next button stays enabled.
- Clicking next sets offset to `user_count` and loads an empty page.

Use `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)` instead.

findings.title: Unbounded/unvalidated limit and offset on public members endpoint
findings.body:
`limit` and `offset` come straight from params with no bounds. This endpoint is public (any user who can see the group).

- A very large limit (e.g. `limit=10000000`) serializes the entire membership of huge automatic groups like trust_level_0 in one request, which is a cheap DoS vector.
- A negative limit or offset is passed to Postgres, which rejects negative LIMIT/OFFSET and raises a 500.

Clamp limit to a sane range (e.g. 1..200) and offset to >= 0.

findings.title: Public group members page now silently truncated to 50 members
findings.body:
`findMembers` now requests a page of 50 (the model default limit). The public `group/members.hbs` template has no pagination controls, so users can no longer see anyone beyond the first 50 members.

Previously, non-automatic groups returned all members. This is a functional regression for the public group page; it needs paging/infinite scroll, or a larger limit.

findings.title: Adding an existing member likely raises instead of being ignored
findings.body:
`add_members` calls `group.add(user)` for every username without checking membership. If any of the usernames is already a member, the insert into group_users can violate the unique (group_id, user_id) constraint. That raises an exception and returns a 500.

In that case none of the success handling runs, and the users processed before the duplicate are already persisted, leaving a partial update. Skip users who are already members (e.g. `group.users.include?(user)`, or `where.not(id: group.user_ids)`).

findings.title: Spec uses PUT for remove_member which is routed as DELETE
findings.body: The "cannot remove members from automatic groups" spec issues `xhr :put, :remove_member`, but the route defines `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"`. The test does not exercise the actual HTTP verb clients use. Use `xhr :delete` for consistency with the route and the other spec.

findings.title: Username input not cleared after adding members
findings.body: After `addMembers` succeeds, `usernames` is never reset (the code acknowledges this with a TODO). The selected users remain in the selector, and clicking Add again re-submits the same usernames. Clear `usernames` in the promise's `then`.

findings.title: create ignores alias_level sent by the client
findings.body: The client's `asJSON` sends `alias_level` on create, but `create` only assigns `name` and `visible`. Any alias level chosen when creating a new group is silently dropped until the group is saved a second time.
